episodes.title: Responding to objections to recursive self-improvement
episodes.about: Dwarkesh responds to the strongest objections to his recursive self-improvement essay, working through named critics on whether AI research is a verifiable domain, whether AI's success in math transfers to AI research, whether many different models would constrain each other, and whether AI research will be bottlenecked on compute.
episodes.why: Dwarkesh answers the strongest objections to his RSI essay — whether AI research is verifiable, whether math success transfers, and whether compute bottlenecks the loop.

episodes.title: AI Just Made History in the Middle of a Meltdown
episodes.about: Claude may have helped prove the Riemann hypothesis just as the Nvidia scandal and Anthropic's IPO are fueling a backlash over who profits from AI and who gets to call the shots. In the headlines: Grok falls behind and Z.ai previews GLM 5.4.
episodes.why: Claude may have helped prove the Riemann hypothesis while the Nvidia scandal and Anthropic's IPO fuel a backlash over who profits; plus Grok falling behind and Z.ai's GLM 5.4 preview.

episodes.title: Building AI That Can Reason Under Uncertainty with Thore Graepel
episodes.about: Thore Graepel, CEO and co-founder of Metis Reasoning and Chair of Machine Learning at UCL, explores an approach to AI reasoning inspired by his work on AlphaGo. He argues reliable reasoning requires explicit representations of knowledge and uncertainty, with language models helping to generate hypotheses and interpret evidence, and explains how a system could break down complex questions, gather evidence, and choose its next step based on the uncertainty it expects to resolve.
episodes.why: Thore Graepel, who worked on AlphaGo, argues reliable reasoning needs explicit representations of uncertainty — not just a language model guessing — and shows how a system would gather evidence step by step.

episodes.title: Why Transparency Matters for AI Security | NVIDIA AI Podcast Ep. 304
episodes.about: Red Hat CTO Chris Wright joins the NVIDIA AI Podcast at GTC Berlin to explain why open source is the foundation for secure AI agents. From Linux in the 1990s to agent security today, he shares what has changed, what hasn't, and why governance is what made us go faster.
episodes.why: Discovery pick — NVIDIA AI Podcast is NVIDIA's interview show, new to this list; Red Hat CTO Chris Wright at GTC Berlin on why open source and governance are the foundation for secure AI agents.

episodes.title: Can AI spark a new wave of entrepreneurship? | Reid Hoffman
episodes.about: What happens to economic opportunity when AI changes the jobs people rely on? Reid Hoffman and Aria Finger explore why entrepreneurial skills will matter in every career and how AI can help more people start businesses. Reid traces his focus on expanding access to good jobs from founding LinkedIn to working with Opportunity@Work, including opportunities for workers without college degrees.
episodes.why: Reid Hoffman and Aria Finger on whether AI lowers the cost of starting a business enough to widen who gets to try — and why entrepreneurial skills matter in jobs that aren't founder jobs. Sixteen minutes, out this morning.
